title: Agent and Multi-Agent Patterns
tagline: Choose the loop, the crew, the context and the memory on purpose.
story: One model call is no longer enough: the question needs several steps, some tools and maybe several specialists. Every step you add costs tokens and latency and adds a new way to fail. Here you learn to add autonomy only when it earns its cost, and to keep the context, the memory and the run alive long enough to finish.
oneLiner: Start at the lowest rung of autonomy that works, then climb only when a dial you can name forces you to.
youWillLearn: Place a task on the autonomy dial: single call, workflow, agent or multi-agent
Pick among chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer by task structure and risk
Run ReAct, plan-and-execute and reflection loops with hard brakes on steps, tokens and repeated calls
Compare supervisor, handoff, group chat and Magentic topologies, and weigh the single versus multi-agent evidence
Budget a context window with clearing, compaction, offloading and sub-agent isolation, and explain context rot
Design memory with explicit write and read policies and defend it against poisoning and privacy failures
Keep long-running agents alive with checkpoints, idempotency keys, human approval waits and budgets

flashcards.front: What separates a **workflow** from an **agent** in Anthropic's definition?
flashcards.back: Workflows orchestrate LLMs and tools through predefined code paths. In an agent the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use. Both are agentic systems.

flashcards.front: State Microsoft's rule for choosing a rung of the complexity ladder.
flashcards.back: Use the lowest level of complexity that reliably meets your requirements: direct model call, then single agent with tools, then multiagent orchestration.

flashcards.front: Name the five workflow patterns from Anthropic's guide.
flashcards.back: Prompt chaining, routing, parallelization (sectioning and voting), orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer, all built on an augmented LLM.

flashcards.front: When does evaluator-optimizer pay off?
flashcards.back: When clear evaluation criteria exist and revision measurably helps. Without criteria or an external signal the critic drifts and the loop burns tokens.

flashcards.front: ReAct in one line, and its reported gain?
flashcards.back: Interleave reasoning traces with actions and observations. On ALFWorld and WebShop it beat imitation and RL baselines by an absolute 34% and 10% success rate.

flashcards.front: What does **ReWOO** change compared with ReAct?
flashcards.back: It plans the tool calls first and runs them without interleaved reasoning. The paper reports 5x token efficiency and 4% higher accuracy on HotpotQA.

flashcards.front: Why does a naive agent loop grow quadratically in steps?
flashcards.back: Each step re-reads the prefix plus all earlier observations. Total input is n times the prefix plus observation size times n(n-1)/2, unless you cache, clear or compact.

flashcards.front: Which loop brakes must live outside the model?
flashcards.back: Step cap, token or cost budget, wall-clock limit and repeated-call detection, each enforced by the harness and each ending the run with an explicit stop reason.

flashcards.front: Handoff versus agent-as-tool: who owns the conversation afterwards?
flashcards.back: Handoff: the receiving agent takes ownership and the full context. Agent-as-tool: the caller keeps ownership and regains control when the tool returns.

flashcards.front: What token multipliers did Anthropic report for agents and multi-agent systems?
flashcards.back: About 4x the tokens of chat for agents and about 15x for multi-agent systems, vendor-reported on its own research traffic. Value per task must justify that cost.

flashcards.front: How did Cognition's view move between 2025-06-12 and 2026-04-22?
flashcards.back: 2025: share full traces, actions carry implicit decisions, prefer one single-threaded agent. 2026: parallel writers still fail, but several agents can contribute while writes stay single-threaded.

flashcards.front: What is **MAST**?
flashcards.back: A taxonomy of 14 multi-agent failure modes in 3 categories: system design, inter-agent misalignment and task verification. It rests on 1600+ annotated traces from 7 frameworks.

flashcards.front: What is **context rot**?
flashcards.back: Quality falls as input grows, unevenly and well below advertised windows. In NoLiMa, 11 of 13 models claiming 128K or more fell under 50% of their short-context baseline at 32K.

flashcards.front: Which compaction step does Anthropic call one of the safest and lightest?
flashcards.back: Tool result clearing: drop stale tool outputs deep in history while keeping the call record and a restorable pointer such as a path or URL.

flashcards.front: Why does a timestamp at the start of a system prompt hurt an agent?
flashcards.back: Prompt caches match an identical prefix. A changing first token invalidates everything after it. Keep prefixes stable, context append-only and serialisation deterministic.

flashcards.front: Which memory types does the CoALA framework distinguish?
flashcards.back: Working memory, plus long-term procedural, semantic and episodic memory.

flashcards.front: Foundry Agent Service memory: types, status and key limits as of 2026-10-13?
flashcards.back: Preview. User profile, chat summary and procedural memory via extraction, consolidation and retrieval. 100 scopes per store, 10,000 memories per scope, no VNet integration.

flashcards.front: How can an attacker poison agent memory without write access?
flashcards.back: MINJA plants malicious records through ordinary queries and outputs. AgentPoison backdoors long-term memory or RAG stores at a poison rate under 0.1%. Treat every write as untrusted.

flashcards.front: Checkpoint versus durable execution?
flashcards.back: A checkpoint lets a run resume. Side effects still need idempotency keys or compensating steps, and replay needs deterministic orchestration code.

flashcards.front: What does a Microsoft Agent Framework workflow checkpoint capture?
flashcards.back: At the end of each superstep: executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses, and shared state.

flashcards.front: Which rules govern an idempotency key for a retried tool call?
flashcards.back: Generate it once per logical operation, client side, and reuse it on every retry. Stripe allows up to 255 characters and may prune v1 keys after 24 hours.

glossary.def: How much of the control flow the model decides: none (single call), fixed code paths (workflow), or its own loop (agent).
LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths. The developer owns the control flow.
A system where the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use. The model owns the control flow.
The building block of agentic systems: a model with retrieval, tools and memory.
A lead model decides subtasks at run time, delegates them to workers and synthesises the results.
Transfer of the conversation to another agent that takes ownership. In the OpenAI Agents SDK a handoff is exposed to the model as a tool named `transfer_to_<agent_name>` by default.
A specialist agent called like a function. The caller keeps ownership and receives control back with the result.
A manager agent keeps shared context and a task ledger, tracks progress and re-plans. Based on the Magentic-One design.
The manager's running record of facts, plan and progress in Magentic orchestration.
Degradation of model quality as input length grows, observed below advertised context windows.
Shrinking context by summarising, clearing stale tool results or offloading content, ideally with a restorable pointer.
Giving a worker its own clean window and returning only a short result, so exploration noise stays out of the lead's context.
Records of specific past events or interactions, retrieved when a similar situation recurs.
Stored how-to knowledge such as rules, instructions or workflow steps, retrieved for recurring tasks.
One round of a Microsoft Agent Framework workflow. A checkpoint is written at the end of each one.
A client-generated identifier reused on retries so a repeated request returns the saved result instead of repeating the side effect.

claims.text: Anthropic defines workflows as LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths and agents as systems where the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use. The post is dated 2024-12-19.
Anthropic's guide names five workflow patterns on top of an augmented LLM: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization (sectioning and voting), orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer.

Microsoft's architecture guidance lists three levels (direct model call, single agent with tools, multiagent orchestration) and says to use the lowest level of complexity that reliably meets your requirements.
ReAct beat imitation and RL baselines by an absolute 34% and 10% success rate on ALFWorld and WebShop with one or two in-context examples.
Reflexion reports 91% pass@1 on HumanEval against 80% for the GPT-4 baseline.
ReWOO reports 5x token efficiency and 4% higher accuracy on HotpotQA compared with interleaved reasoning.
OpenAI says reasoning-capable GPT-5 models usually work best with a clear goal, strong constraints and an explicit output contract, without prescribing every intermediate step.

In Microsoft Agent Framework, handoff is a mesh with no central orchestrator, the receiving agent takes full ownership and context, and handoff supports Agent only with local tool execution. The Azure guide (r9) lists infinite handoff loops and excessive bouncing as a challenge.
In the OpenAI Agents SDK a handoff is exposed to the model as a tool whose default name is transfer_to_<agent_name>.

Magentic orchestration keeps shared context and a task ledger in a manager. Microsoft says it is untested how well it performs outside the original Magentic-One design, and the C# types are experimental.

Anthropic reports agents use about 4x and multi-agent systems about 15x the tokens of chat, that its multi-agent system beat single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal research eval, and that token usage explained 80% of BrowseComp variance.
Anthropic reports parallel subagents and tool calls cut research time by up to 90%, and that synchronous subagents created bottlenecks. The post is dated 2025-06-13.
Cognition's 2025-06-12 post argues against parallel multi-agent designs because actions carry implicit decisions that conflict.

Cognition's 2026-04-22 post says parallel-writer swarms still fail while multiple agents can contribute with single-threaded writes, and reports Devin Review catching on average 2 bugs per pull request, about 58% severe.
MAST defines 14 multi-agent failure modes in 3 categories (system design issues, inter-agent misalignment, task verification) with 1600+ annotated traces across 7 frameworks.
OpenAI advises maximizing a single agent first and splitting when prompts hold many if-then-else branches or tool selection fails after clearer tool descriptions.
In NoLiMa, 11 of 13 models claiming 128K or more fell below 50% of their short-context baseline at 32K, and GPT-4o dropped from 99.3% to 69.7%.
RULER tested 17 models and found only about half keep satisfactory performance at 32K despite claiming 32K or more.

Anthropic's context editing is beta with header context-management-2025-06-27 and strategies clear_tool_uses_20250919 (optional clear_tool_inputs) and clear_thinking_20251015. The page says server-side compaction is now the primary strategy.

Manus calls KV-cache hit rate the single most important production metric, quotes cached input at $0.30 versus $3 per million tokens uncached on 2025-07-18, and reports an average input to output token ratio of about 100:1.

Foundry Agent Service memory is in preview with user profile, chat summary and procedural types, limits of 100 scopes per store and 10,000 memories per scope, 1,000 search and 1,000 update requests per minute, and no VNet integration.
AgentPoison reports average attack success above 80% at a poison rate below 0.1%, and MINJA plants malicious memory records through ordinary queries with no direct write access.
Mem0 reports 91% lower p95 latency and over 90% token-cost savings against a full-context baseline on LOCOMO in a vendor-authored paper.

Agent Framework workflow checkpoints are written at the end of each superstep and capture executor state, pending messages, pending requests and responses, and shared state. From Python 1.13.0 an entry checkpoint is also written before the first superstep.

The Durable Extension for Agent Framework makes human-in-the-loop waits consume no compute and no model tokens, installs with a prerelease flag (--prerelease for .NET, --pre for pip) and states no GA status as of 2026-10-13.
In OpenAI background mode you poll the response until it leaves queued and in_progress, and without an explicit store=true a background response is deleted after roughly 10 minutes.
Stripe idempotency keys are client-generated, up to 255 characters, and v1 keys can be pruned after at least 24 hours.

Anthropic's long-running harness uses an initializer agent that creates init.sh, claude-progress.txt and a first git commit. Failure modes were trying to one-shot the app and declaring the job done too early.

Anthropic Managed Agents separates session, harness and sandbox, resumes a failed harness with wake(sessionId), and uses beta header managed-agents-2026-04-01 (the beta status and header are in the Managed Agents docs overview, the wake(sessionId) detail is in the post).
